cards.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, is writing to God's chosen people scattered across Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia, and he's just told them about an inheritance kept in heaven for them that's imperishable, undefiled and unfading (1 Peter 1:1, 4). Now he tells them how to live: prepare your minds for action and be sober-minded. That's not the snooze button, friend, that's both feet on the floor with the apron already ON.

cards.question: Peter wants their minds ready and clear. Where does he tell them to set their hope fully?

answers.text: On the grace coming when Jesus Christ is revealed
On the day their years of hardship finally end
On the reward their faithful work will earn them

cards.text: Then Peter calls them obedient children and brings up the passions of their former ignorance. You know, the stuff we look back on and go, "Why did I think that was a GOOD idea?"

cards.question: Peter tells these obedient children to keep shaping their lives around the passions of their former ignorance.

cards.text: So instead, Peter sets the bar: be holy in all you do. Not some of the batches, friend, not MOST of the batches, ALL of them, even the lopsided last one off the tray.

cards.question: Peter backs up his call to be holy with Scripture. Why should they be holy?

answers.text: Because the One who called them is holy
Because their neighbors are watching them closely
Because being holy keeps their troubles away

cards.text: Then Peter reminds them who they call on: a Father who judges each one's work impartially. Everybody's work gets the same fair look, friend, no favorites.

cards.question: Their Father judges each one's work impartially. So how does Peter tell them to conduct themselves?
Peter tells them to live in reverent fear during their stay as ___.

cards.text: Peter reminds them they were redeemed from the empty way of life handed down from their forefathers. That's like inheriting the family recipe box, opening it up, and finding nothing but the box.

cards.question: Peter says they were not redeemed with perishable things like silver or gold.
Not silver and not gold. So what does Peter say they were redeemed with?

cards.text: Peter describes Christ as a lamb without blemish or spot.
Peter says Christ was known before the foundation of the world. Before the WORLD, friend, and I can't even pick a batch before the oven starts beeping at me.

cards.question: Christ was known before the foundation of the world. When was He revealed, and for whose sake?

answers.text: In the last times for their sake
In the days of Moses for Israel's sake
At the very beginning for the angels' sake

cards.question: Through Christ they believe in God, who raised Him from the dead and glorified Him. So Peter says their faith and ___ are in God.

cards.text: Next, Peter turns to how they treat each other: they've purified their souls by obeying the truth, so that they have a genuine love for their brothers. GENUINE, friend, not the "we should totally get together sometime" kind.

cards.question: Peter says they purified their souls so they'd have a genuine love for their brothers. So what does he tell them to do?

answers.text: Love one another deeply from a pure heart
Keep their love within their own households
Share their love with those who love them back

cards.text: Peter says they've been born again, not of perishable seed but of imperishable. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer before I was made new, and let me tell you, new beats the drawer EVERY time.

cards.question: Peter says this new birth came through something. What is it?

answers.text: The living and enduring word of God
The faithful work of the apostles
The long line of their forefathers

cards.text: Then Peter quotes Isaiah 40:6-8: all flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flowers of the field. That's everybody, friend, me included, and I'm counting this mustache as GLORY.

cards.question: In the Scripture Peter quotes, the grass and the flowers of the field last forever.
The grass withers and the flowers fall. What does the Scripture Peter quotes say about the word of the Lord?

cards.text: Then Peter adds: "And this is the word that was proclaimed to you." The word that stands forever, friend, and somebody brought it right to THEM.
